name: SendHQ
summary: Email API for developers with transactional and marketing plans, verified-domain sending, inbound email, delivery events and hosted templates.
best_for: developers and small product teams that want a simple email API with fixed monthly plans and no overage billing, and that keep bounce and complaint rates low
skip_if: you need a free tier, pay-as-you-go overage instead of a hard cap, or a high-volume plan above 200,000 emails a month
honest_knock: There is no free plan, only a 100-delivery trial to your own address. The monthly allowance is a hard cap: further sends are rejected, not billed. Sending is limited per sender address and paused automatically at the published bounce and complaint rates, and a pause stops sending for the whole workspace until support reviews it.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter Transactional · Starter Transactional billed monthly, 50,000 emails a month and 25 verified domains
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-06 on sendhq.cc/pricing) SendHQ sells an email API in two plans, each for transactional or for marketing email. Starter costs $9 a month for transactional email or $19 a month for marketing email and includes 50,000 emails a month and 25 verified domains. Scale costs $39 a month for either type and includes 200,000 emails a month and 100 verified domains, plus priority support. Annual billing is 10% off twelve monthly payments: $97.20 a year for Starter Transactional, $205.20 for Starter Marketing and $421.20 for Scale. Every To, Cc and Bcc address counts as one email, and there are no automatic overage charges: once the monthly allowance is used, further sends are rejected until the next month or until you move to a larger plan. There is no free plan; new workspaces get a trial of 100 deliveries to your own account email or a test address. Plans are billed in USD, and stablecoins (USDC) are accepted on every plan.

claims.claim: Rows marked unsubscribed in your file come in as unsubscribed and never get broadcasts.

claims.buying_consequence: Automatic custom fields do not establish two native tags or binary attachments.

claims.claim: Recorded on every contact as evidence of consent.

claims.buying_consequence: A mandatory basis entry records the supplied explanation; it does not establish opt-in or permission to send.

Tags remained a single text field and attachment remained filename text.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 2 November 2026 on the unpaid integration trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported two fictional contacts from a CSV file, then ran a second import to update one of them. We sent nothing, created no API key and did not open checkout.
findings: The trial shows 'Integration trial', 'No active subscription' and 100 recipient deliveries (0 of 100 used). No card was asked for. The plan page lists Transactional Starter at $9 a month, Marketing Starter at $19 and Scale at $39 a month, with a 10% annual discount and the note 'Hard monthly caps, no overage bills.'
Contacts accepts a CSV of up to 5,000 rows and 5 MB, and nothing is imported until you confirm. Name and email columns matched on their own. Every other column became a custom contact field.
The import asks why you may email these people and requires an answer. Our records were synthetic, so we said so; the answer is stored on each contact as evidence of consent.

Our test file marked one contact 'blocked'. SendHQ did not recognise that word and showed both rows as subscribed in the preview. After we changed the value to 'unsubscribed', the preview showed zero subscribed and both contacts arrived as unsubscribed.

The accented name, the e-mail address and the two-line note came through unchanged. The pipe-separated tag 'aibm-test|alpha' stayed one text value instead of two tags. A file name in the attachment column is stored as plain text; contacts have no file upload.

A second import with 'Update names and fields of contacts who already exist' ticked reported New 0 and Existing 2. The changed note on the second contact updated and the first stayed as it was. Contacts are matched on the e-mail address, not on an ID.
not_tested: Export: we found no export or download button on Contacts or Lists, so we could not check what a file would contain. That is not a finding that SendHQ has no export
A round trip with native record IDs, and any check of attachments
Checkout, tax and the final price: the browser session did not allow opening it
Support, team roles, invitations, downgrade and cancellation
Sending: we sent no message and created no API key or sending domain
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
